Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments

Inglewood, California
  November 7, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  November 7, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Padilla, Morales,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Gray.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  November 3, 2023, in the amount of $5,575,859.77, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Gray.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 24-039 APPROVED – STATE OF CALLIFORNIA FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-2024 OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY GRANT; RESOLUTION NO.
  24-11 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDDGET. Staff
  report dated November 7, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members approve an agreement with the State of California for acceptance of the Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 Office of Traffic Safety Grant.
 November 7, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 24-039 in the total amount of
  $270,000; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-11 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FUNDS
  FROM THE OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY IN THE AMOUNT OF $270,000

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

103.3  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-040 APPROVED – HHJ
  CONSTRUCTION, INC (HHJ); CITY CONTROLLED CONTINGENCY
  APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 24-12 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2023/2024
  ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated November 7, 2023, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve an Agreement with HHJ
  Construction, Inc. (HHJ) to provide residential sound insulation work on 81 residential units
  (RSI Phase XV, Group 37).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award a contract and approve Agreement No. 24-040 in
  an amount not to exceed $1,920,000; 2) Approve a City controlled and directed 10%
  contingency of $192,000, and special expense of $31,590, per Bid No. CB-23-20; and 3)
  Adopt Resolution No. 24-12 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023/2024 ANNUAL BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 24-13 ADOPTED - AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER
  OR HIS DESIGNEE TO SIGN THE MATERIALS RELASE WAIVER AND ANY
  FUTURE AND SIMILAR NO-COST WAIVERS UPON REVIEW AND APPROVAL
  BY THE OFFICE OF THE CITY ATTORNEY FROM ENTERTAINMENT ONE
  REALITY PRODUCTIONS, LLC, FOR USE OF THE CITY SEAL IN THE
  DOCUMENTARY ON THE LIFE OF BECKY G. Staff report dated November 7, 2023,
  was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution 1)
  authorizing the City Manager or Designee to sign the Materials Release Waiver from
  Entertainment One Reality Productions, LLC, for use of the City Seal in the documentary
  on the life of Becky G; and 2) authorizing the City Manager or Designee to sign any future
  and similar no-cost waivers for use of the City Seal upon review and approval by the Office
  of the City Attorney.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  Resolution No. 24-13 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER OR HIS DESIGNEE
  TO SIGN A RELEASE REGARDING THE CITY SEAL’S INCLUSION IN
  MEDIA

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  2
 November 7, 2023

  * The Closed Session Item matter has been reconvened from the special meeting held on
  November 7, 2023, at 8:30 a.m.
132.9  CLOSED SESSION – PERSONNEL EXEMPTION – SELECTION OF AN
  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER. Closed Session – Confidential – Personnel Exemption;
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957(b)(1); Selection of an Assistant City Manager.
  Interviews were provided; Information given to the City Manager.

101  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Artie Fields reported that he had
  appointed Jose Cortes as Assistant City Manager. He asked that everyone join in to
  congratulate Jose Cortes.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson congratulated the newly
  appointed Assistant City Manager, Jose Cortes. She stated that she looked forward to
  working with him, and his appointment was well deserved and earned. The City Clerk
  reported being honored to speak at the Alpha Kappa Alpha (AKA) Chapter meeting,  where
  she provided information about voting. She mentioned the ladies of AKA were interested in
  getting involved with some of the activities going on in the City, going to schools, and working
  with the youth. The City Clerk thanked Ms. Williams for allowing her to stand before the women
  of AKA, and it was an honor. In her report, she also  mentioned that she visited Inglewood
  High School’s Government class and thanked Mr. O’Cain for allowing her to speak to his class
  to encourage them to register to vote.  Additionally, she added that she and the Mayor
  would attend Morningside High School  the following week to speak with their Government
  class. Furthermore, she paid homage to all the Veterans who served and wished Daniel Medina
  from the Parks and Recreation  Department a Happy Birthday.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at the hour of 2:04 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at the hour of 2:05 p.m.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Yolanda Davidson addressed the issue of crime in the City of Inglewood. She stated that
  there have been several shootings in the City, and there is no active gang task force
  presently. She added that someone was recently murdered, and more public safety was
  needed. She also addressed several residents being afraid and her teenage daughter when
  she’s out late at night. Finally, she also stated that things occur in daylight and reiterated
  the need for more public safety.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:16 p.m.

  Approved this 12th day of December, 2023.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
